sentences.zh: 于義于義，字慈恭，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yu Yi, styled Cigong, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, whose courtesy name was Cigong, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父謹，從魏武帝入關，仕周，官至太師，因家京兆。

translations.literal: His father Jin followed Emperor Wu of Wei in entering the pass, served Zhou, reached the post of Grand Preceptor, and thus made his home in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Jin had followed Yuwen Tai into the pass, served the Northern Zhou, rose to Grand Preceptor, and established the family in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 義少矜嚴，有操尚，篤志好學。

translations.literal: Yi from youth was stern and dignified, had integrity and aspiration, and devotedly loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Yi was solemn and self-restrained, held to high standards, and pursued his studies with steadfast devotion.

sentences.zh: 大統末，以父功，賜爵平昌縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: At the end of the Datong era, on his father's merit, he was granted the title Marquis of Pingchang County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Datong reign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingchang on his father's merit, with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 起家直閤將軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as General of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as General of the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 其後改封廣都縣公。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Guangdu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was later re-enfeoffed as Duke of Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝受禪，增邑六百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Zhou received the abdication, his fief was increased by six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Zhou took the throne, his fief was increased by six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 累遷安武太守，專崇德教，不尚威刑。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to Governor of Anwu, focusing exclusively on moral instruction and not prizing stern punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Governor of Anwu, where he devoted himself to moral instruction rather than harsh punishments.

sentences.zh: 有郡民張善安、王叔兒爭財相訟，義曰：「太守德薄不勝任之所致，非其罪也。

translations.literal: When subjects Zhang Shan'an and Wang Shu'er sued one another over property, Yi said: "This comes from the inadequacy of the governor's virtue and his inability to fulfill the role—it is not their fault."
translations.idiomatic: When two local men, Zhang Shan'an and Wang Shu'er, went to court over a property dispute, Yi said, "This stems from my own deficient virtue and my failure to govern well—it is not their fault."

sentences.zh: 」於是取家財，倍與二人，喻而遣去。

translations.literal: He then took from his own wealth, doubled what he gave to the two men, instructed them, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He then took from his own household goods, doubled what he gave each of them, reasoned with them, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 善安等各懷恥愧，移貫他州。

translations.literal: Shan'an and the others each felt shame and moved their registrations to other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Shan'an and the others each transferred their household registration to another prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於是風教大洽。

translations.literal: Thereupon custom and teaching were widely harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: From that point custom and moral instruction spread widely through the commandery.

sentences.zh: 其以德化人，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His winning people through virtue was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His way of winning people through virtue was always of this sort.

sentences.zh: 進封建平郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Jianping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 明、武世，歷西京、瓜、邵三州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Ming and Wu reigns he served in succession as governor of the three prefectures Xijing, Guazhou, and Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ming and Wu he served in turn as governor of Xijing, Guazhou, and Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 數從征伐，進位開府。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed on campaigns and was promoted to the rank of open mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in many campaigns and was promoted to the rank of Open Mansion.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，政刑日亂，義上疏諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, government and punishments grew daily chaotic; Yi submitted a memorial of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuan came to the throne, government and punishments grew more chaotic by the day, and Yi submitted a memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 時鄭譯、劉昉以恩幸當權，謂義不利於己，先惡之於帝。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Yi and Liu Fang held power through favor; believing Yi was harmful to them, they first slandered him to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zheng Yi and Liu Fang held power through imperial favor; seeing Yi as a threat, they blackened his name with the emperor first.

sentences.zh: 帝覽表色動，謂侍臣曰：「于義謗訕朝廷也。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial, his expression changed, and he told the attending officials: "Yu Yi is slandering the court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial, his expression changed, and he told those attending him, "Yu Yi is slandering the court."

sentences.zh: 」禦正大夫顏之儀進曰：「古先哲王立誹謗之木，置敢諫之鼓，猶懼不聞過。

translations.literal: Attending rectifier Yan Zhiyi stepped forward and said: "The sage kings of old erected a post for accusations and set a drum for bold remonstrance, yet still feared they would not hear of their faults."
translations.idiomatic: Attending Rectifier Yan Zhiyi stepped forward and said, "The sage kings of antiquity set up a post for accusations and a drum for bold remonstrance, yet still feared they would never hear of their faults."

sentences.zh: 于義之言，不可罪也。

translations.literal: Yu Yi's words must not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi's words must not be punished.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor then relented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then relented.

sentences.zh: 及高祖作相，王謙構逆，高祖將擊之，問將于高熲。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke became chancellor, Wang Qian rose in rebellion; the Grand Duke was about to attack him and asked Gao Jiong for a commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became chancellor, Wang Qian raised a rebellion; Yang Jian was about to attack him and asked Gao Jiong whom to appoint as commander.

sentences.zh: 熲答曰：「于義素有經略，可為元帥。

translations.literal: Jiong replied: "Yu Yi has long had strategic ability and may serve as supreme commander."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong replied, "Yu Yi has long possessed strategic talent and can serve as supreme commander."

sentences.zh: 」高祖初然之。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke at first agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian at first agreed.

sentences.zh: 劉昉進曰：「梁睿位望素重，不可居義之下。

translations.literal: Liu Fang advanced and said: "Liang Rui's position and reputation have long been weighty; he cannot stand below Yi."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang stepped forward and said, "Liang Rui's standing and reputation have long been weighty; he cannot be placed beneath Yi."

sentences.zh: 」高祖乃止。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian then dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 於是以睿為元帥，以義為行軍總管。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rui was made supreme commander and Yi marching commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was therefore made supreme commander and Yi marching commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 謙將達奚惎擁眾據開遠，義將左軍擊破之。

translations.literal: Qian's general Daxi Ji massed troops and held Kaiyuan; Yi led the left wing and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's general Daxi Ji gathered a host and held Kaiyuan; Yi led the left wing and routed him.

sentences.zh: 尋拜潼州總管，賜奴婢五百口，雜彩三千段，超拜上柱國。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed overall commander of Tongzhou, given five hundred bondsmen and bondswomen and three thousand lengths of mixed silks, and promoted beyond regular rank to Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed overall commander of Tongzhou, granted five hundred bondsmen and bondswomen and three thousand lengths of patterned silks, and promoted beyond the usual sequence to Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 時義兄翼為太尉，弟智、兄子仲文並上柱國，大將軍已上十餘人，稱為貴戚。

translations.literal: At that time Yi's elder brother Yi was Grand Commandant, his younger brother Zhi and his brother's son Zhongwen were each Senior Pillar of State, and more than ten held the rank of great general or above—they were called the eminent kin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yi's elder brother Yi was Grand Commandant; his younger brother Zhi and his brother's son Zhongwen were each Senior Pillar of State; and more than ten in the family held the rank of great general or above—they were spoken of as the great imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以疾免職，歸於京師。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was relieved on grounds of illness and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was relieved of office on account of illness and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 數月卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: A few months later he died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he died, at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 贈豫州刺史，諡曰剛。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Yuzhou with the posthumous name Gang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Governor of Yuzhou and given the posthumous name Gang (Steadfast).

sentences.zh: 賻物千段，粟米五百石。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts were a thousand lengths of goods and five hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts amounted to a thousand lengths of goods and five hundred piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 子宣道、宣敏，並知名。

translations.literal: His sons Xuandao and Xuanmin were both well known.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xuandao and Xuanmin were both well known.

sentences.zh: 子宣道宣道字元明，性謹密，不交非類。

translations.literal: His son Xuandao, styled Yuanming, was by nature cautious and tight-lipped and did not associate with unworthy sorts.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuandao, whose courtesy name was Yuanming, was cautious and reserved by nature and would not associate with unworthy company.

sentences.zh: 仕周，釋褐左侍上士。

translations.literal: He served Zhou and upon leaving the brown robe was made Left Attendant Superior Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Zhou and, upon leaving the brown robe of a student, was appointed Left Attendant Superior Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 以父功，賜爵成安縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: On his father's merit he was granted the title Baron of Cheng'an County with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Cheng'an, with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後轉小承禦上士。

translations.literal: He was later transferred to Junior Supervisor of the Imperial Carriage, superior gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Junior Supervisor of the Imperial Carriage, superior gentleman.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，引為外兵曹，尋拜儀同。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke was chancellor he was brought in as clerk of external military affairs and soon appointed Companion of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chancellor he was brought in as clerk of external military affairs and soon appointed Companion of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，遷內史舍人，進爵為子。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Xuandao was moved to Secretariat Attendant and advanced in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Xuandao was moved to Secretariat Attendant and advanced in rank to Viscount.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，水漿不入口者累日。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he took mourning and for many days would not take water or food.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his father's death he entered mourning and for many days would take neither food nor drink.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后命中使敦諭，歲餘，起令視事。

translations.literal: Empress Xian ordered palace envoys to urge him earnestly; after more than a year she had him rise and resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xian sent palace envoys to urge him earnestly; after more than a year she had him rise and resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 免喪，拜車騎將軍，兼左衛長史，舍人如故。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and concurrently Chief Clerk of the Left Guard, retaining his attendant post.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and concurrently Chief Clerk of the Left Guard, while retaining his attendant post.

sentences.zh: 後六歲，遷太子左衛副率，進位上儀同。

translations.literal: Six years later he was transferred to Deputy Leader of the Crown Prince's Left Guard and advanced to Senior Companion of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he was transferred to Deputy Leader of the Crown Prince's Left Guard and advanced to Senior Companion of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: He died, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 子志甯，早知名，出繼叔父宣敏。

translations.literal: His son Zhi'ning was early known for reputation and was adopted out to his uncle Xuanmin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi'ning was known early for his reputation and was adopted as heir to his uncle Xuanmin.

sentences.zh: 宣道弟宣敏宣敏字仲達，少沉密，有才思。

translations.literal: Xuandao's younger brother Xuanmin, styled Zhongda, from youth was deep and secretive and had talent and reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandao's younger brother Xuanmin, whose courtesy name was Zhongda, was from youth reserved and thoughtful and possessed real talent.

sentences.zh: 年十一，詣周趙王招，王命之賦詩。

translations.literal: At age eleven he called on the Zhou Prince of Zhao, Zhao, and the prince ordered him to compose a poem.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of eleven he called on Zhao, Prince of Zhao under the Zhou, and the prince ordered him to compose a poem.

sentences.zh: 宣敏為詩，甚有幽貞之志。

translations.literal: Xuanmin composed a poem with very strong aspirations of secluded integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmin composed a poem that showed a strong spirit of secluded integrity.

sentences.zh: 王大奇之，坐客莫不嗟賞。

translations.literal: The prince marveled at it greatly, and none of those seated failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was deeply impressed, and every guest present sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 起家右侍上士，遷千牛備身。

translations.literal: He began his career as Right Attendant Superior Gentleman and was moved to Palace Guard of the Thousand Oxen.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Right Attendant Superior Gentleman and was later transferred to Palace Guard of the Thousand Oxen.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，拜奉車都尉，奉使撫慰巴蜀。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke took the throne he was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and sent on a mission to comfort Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne he was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and sent on a mission to comfort Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 及還，上疏曰：

translations.literal: When he returned he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞開磐石之宗，漢室於是惟永；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that by opening the clan of bedrock, the house of Han was thereby enduring;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that by establishing a bedrock clan, the house of Han was thereby made enduring;

sentences.zh: 建維城之固，周祚所以靈長。

translations.literal: by building the solidity of a protecting wall, the Zhou mandate was thereby numinous and long.
translations.idiomatic: and by building the solid walls of a protecting state, the Zhou mandate was thereby made long-lived.

sentences.zh: 昔秦皇置牧守而罷諸侯，魏後昵諂邪而疏骨肉，遂使宗社移於他族，神器傳於異姓。

translations.literal: Formerly the First Emperor of Qin set governors and prefects and abolished the feudal lords; the Wei successor favored flatterers and estranged his kin, so that the altars of state shifted to another clan and the sacred vessel passed to a different surname.
translations.idiomatic: In former times the First Emperor of Qin appointed governors and abolished the feudal lords; the Wei successor favored flatterers and estranged his own kin, so that the altars of state passed to another clan and the sacred vessel to a different surname.

sentences.zh: 此事之明，甚於觀火。

translations.literal: The clarity of this matter exceeds watching fire.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson is clearer than watching a fire burn.

sentences.zh: 然山川設險，非親勿居。

translations.literal: Yet where mountains and rivers set barriers, none but kin should dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Yet where mountains and rivers form natural barriers, none but kin should be stationed.

sentences.zh: 且蜀土沃饒，人物殷阜，西通邛僰，南屬荊巫。

translations.literal: Moreover the land of Shu is fertile and rich, its people numerous and prosperous; west it connects with Qiong and Bo, south it adjoins Jing and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the land of Shu is fertile and rich, its people numerous and prosperous; to the west it opens on Qiong and Bo, to the south it adjoins Jing and the lands of Wu.

sentences.zh: 周德之衰，茲土遂成戎首；

translations.literal: When Zhou virtue declined, this soil became the head of the barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou virtue declined, this region became the leader of rebellion;

sentences.zh: 炎政失禦，此地便為禍先。

translations.literal: when Han rule lost control, this place became the first of disasters.
translations.idiomatic: when Han government lost its grip, this place became the first seat of calamity.

sentences.zh: 是以明者防於無形，治者制其未亂，方可慶隆萬世，年逾七百。

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened guard against what has no form, the governing restrain what is not yet in disorder—only then may one celebrate grandeur for ten thousand generations and years beyond seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the enlightened guard against trouble before it takes shape, and rulers restrain disorder before it breaks out—only then may one celebrate a grandeur lasting ten thousand generations and a reign beyond seven hundred years.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下日角龍顏，膺樂推之運，參天貳地，居揖讓之期，億兆宅心。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty has the sun-corner and dragon countenance, bears the fortune of the people's willing elevation, matches Heaven and stands second only to Earth, occupies the season of yielding the throne, and the hundred millions rest their hearts upon you.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty bears the marks of the sage ruler, has received the mandate the people willingly pressed upon you, stands equal to Heaven and second only to Earth, has come to the throne through abdication, and the myriad people rest their hearts upon you.

sentences.zh: 百神受職，理須樹建籓屏，封植子孫，繼周、漢之宏圖，改秦、魏之覆軌，抑近習之權勢，崇公族之本枝。

translations.literal: The hundred spirits receive their offices; it is right to plant and establish screen-walls for the realm, enfeoff and nurture sons and grandsons, continue the great designs of Zhou and Han, alter the overturned tracks of Qin and Wei, restrain the power of near favorites, and exalt the root branches of the ducal clan.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred spirits have taken their posts; it is only right to plant screen-walls for the realm and enfeoff your sons and grandsons, to continue the great designs of Zhou and Han and turn aside the overturned paths of Qin and Wei, to restrain the power of intimate favorites and exalt the root branches of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 但三蜀、三齊，古稱天險，分王戚屬，今正其時。

translations.literal: Only the Three Shu and Three Qi, called from antiquity heaven's barriers—to divide them among royal kin is exactly the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Shu and Three Qi, called from antiquity heaven's own barriers, should now be divided among your royal kin—the time is exactly right.

sentences.zh: 若使利建合宜，封樹得所，巨猾息其非望，奸臣杜其邪謀。

translations.literal: If profitable establishment suits the measure and enfeoffment and planting find their proper places, great villains will quiet their improper ambitions and treacherous ministers will block their wicked schemes.
translations.idiomatic: If enfeoffments are wisely placed and fiefs properly assigned, great villains will abandon their improper ambitions and treacherous ministers will be cut off from their wicked schemes.

sentences.zh: 盛業洪基，同天地之長久；

translations.literal: A flourishing enterprise and a great foundation will be as long-lasting as Heaven and Earth;
translations.idiomatic: Your flourishing enterprise and great foundation will endure as long as Heaven and Earth;

sentences.zh: 英聲茂實，齊日月之照臨。

translations.literal: illustrious fame and abundant achievement will equal the illumination of sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: your illustrious fame and abundant achievement will shine with sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 臣雖學謝多聞，然情深體國，輒申管見，戰灼惟深。

translations.literal: Your subject, though learning falls short of wide hearing, yet feels deep affection for the body of the state and ventures to set forth a narrow view, trembling and anxious in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Though my learning falls far short of wide knowledge, my devotion to the state runs deep; I venture to offer this narrow view, trembling with the utmost anxiety.

sentences.zh: 帝省表嘉之，謂高熲曰：「於氏世有人焉。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and praised it, saying to Gao Jiong: "Generation after generation the Yu family produces men."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and praised it, saying to Gao Jiong, "Generation after generation the Yu family produces men of talent."

sentences.zh: 」竟納其言，遣蜀王秀鎮於蜀。

translations.literal: He at last adopted the counsel and sent Prince Xiu of Shu to garrison Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He at last adopted the counsel and sent Prince Xiu of Shu to garrison Shu.

sentences.zh: 宣敏常以盛滿之誡，昔賢所重，每懷靜退，著《述志賦》以見其志焉。

translations.literal: Xuanmin often took to heart the warning against reaching the brim that former worthies valued; he constantly wished for quiet withdrawal and wrote "Rhapsody on Stating My Intent" to show his aim.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmin often took to heart the warning against reaching the brim, which former worthies prized; he constantly wished for quiet withdrawal and wrote "Rhapsody on Stating My Intent" to express his mind.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官，時年二十九。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office, aged twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office, at the age of twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 陰壽陰壽，字羅雲，武威人也。

translations.literal: Yin Shou, styled Luoyun, was a native of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shou, whose courtesy name was Luoyun, came from Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 父嵩，周夏州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Song was Governor of Xiazhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Song had served as Governor of Xiazhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 壽少果烈，有武幹，性謹厚，敦然諾。

translations.literal: Shou from youth was decisive and fierce, had military capacity, was by nature cautious and generous, and honored his word.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shou was decisive and fierce, possessed real military talent, was cautious and generous by nature, and kept his word scrupulously.

sentences.zh: 周世屢以軍功，拜儀同。

translations.literal: Under Zhou he repeatedly on military merit was appointed Companion of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he was repeatedly appointed Companion of the Heir on account of military merit.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，進位開府，賜物千段，奴婢百口，女樂二十人。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, he was promoted to open mansion and given a thousand lengths of goods, a hundred bondsmen and bondswomen, and twenty female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi, he was promoted to Open Mansion and granted a thousand lengths of goods, a hundred bondsmen and bondswomen, and twenty female musicians.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，引壽為掾。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke became chancellor he brought Shou in as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became chancellor he brought Shou in as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 尉迥作亂，高祖以韋孝寬為元帥擊之，令壽監軍。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Yong rose in rebellion, the Grand Duke made Wei Xiaokuan supreme commander to attack him and ordered Shou to oversee the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Yong rose in rebellion, Yang Jian appointed Wei Xiaokuan supreme commander to attack him and ordered Shou to oversee the army.

sentences.zh: 時孝寬有疾，不能親總戎事，每臥帳中，遣婦人傳教命。

translations.literal: At that time Xiaokuan was ill and could not personally direct military affairs; he lay each day in his tent and sent women to transmit his orders.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiaokuan was ill and could not personally direct military affairs; he lay in his tent and sent women to relay his orders.

sentences.zh: 三軍綱紀，皆取決於壽。

translations.literal: The army's rules and discipline all depended on Shou.
translations.idiomatic: The army's discipline and command all depended on Shou.

sentences.zh: 以功進位上柱國。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 尋以行軍總管鎮幽州，即拜幽州總管，封趙國公。

translations.literal: Soon as marching commander-in-chief he garrisoned Youzhou and was at once appointed overall commander of Youzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as marching commander-in-chief, he garrisoned Youzhou; he was at once appointed overall commander of Youzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 時有高寶甯者，齊氏之疏屬也，為人桀黠，有籌算，在齊久鎮黃龍。

translations.literal: At that time there was Gao Baoning, a distant kin of the Qi house, crafty and cunning by nature, skilled in reckoning; under Qi he had long garrisoned Huanglong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Gao Baoning, a distant member of the Qi imperial house, crafty and cunning by nature and skilled in calculation; under Qi he had long garrisoned Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 及齊滅，周武帝拜為營州刺史，甚得華夷之心。

translations.literal: When Qi was destroyed Emperor Wu of Zhou appointed him Governor of Yingzhou and he won the hearts of both Chinese and non-Chinese deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou appointed him Governor of Yingzhou, and he won the hearts of both Chinese and non-Chinese subjects.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，遂連結契丹、靺鞨舉兵反。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke was chancellor, Baoning then linked the Khitan and Mohe and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became chancellor, Baoning linked the Khitan and Mohe and raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 高祖以中原多故，未遑進討，以書喻之而不得。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke, with many troubles in the central plains, had no leisure to advance in attack; he sent letters to instruct him but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: With many troubles in the central plains, Yang Jian had no leisure to march against him; he sent letters of persuasion but could not move him.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，又引突厥攻圍北平。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he again drew the Turks to attack and besiege Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang reign he again drew the Turks to attack and besiege Beiping.

sentences.zh: 至是，令壽率步騎數萬，出盧龍塞以討之。

translations.literal: At this point he ordered Shou to lead several tens of thousands of foot and horse out through Lulong Pass to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he ordered Shou to lead several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry out through Lulong Pass to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 寶甯求救於突厥。

translations.literal: Baoning sought rescue from the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Baoning sought rescue from the Turks.

sentences.zh: 時衛王爽等諸將數道北征，突厥不能援。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Wei Shuang and other generals were campaigning north on several routes; the Turks could not aid him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Wei Shuang and other generals were campaigning north on several routes, and the Turks could not come to his aid.

sentences.zh: 寶甯棄城奔於磧北，黃龍諸縣悉平。

translations.literal: Baoning abandoned the city and fled north of the desert; all the counties of Huanglong were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Baoning abandoned the city and fled north of the desert; all the counties of Huanglong were pacified.

sentences.zh: 壽班師，留開府成道昂鎮之。

translations.literal: Shou withdrew the army and left open-mansion holder Cheng Dao'ang to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: Shou withdrew his army and left Open Mansion holder Cheng Dao'ang to garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 寶寧遣其子僧伽率輕騎掠城下而去。

translations.literal: Baoning sent his son Sengqie leading light cavalry to raid below the walls and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Baoning sent his son Sengqie at the head of light cavalry to raid below the walls and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 尋引契丹、靺鞨之眾來攻，道昂苦戰連日乃退。

translations.literal: Soon he led Khitan and Mohe masses to attack; Dao'ang fought bitterly for many days before they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he led Khitan and Mohe forces to attack; Dao'ang fought bitterly for many days before they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 壽患之，於是重購寶寧，又遣人陰間其所親任者趙世模、王威等。

translations.literal: Shou was troubled by this; he therefore set a heavy price on Baoning's head and also sent men secretly to sow discord among those he trusted, Zhao Shimo and Wang Wei and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was troubled by this; he therefore set a heavy price on Baoning's head and also sent men secretly to sow discord among those Baoning trusted, including Zhao Shimo and Wang Wei.

sentences.zh: 月餘，世模率其眾降，寶寧復走契丹，為其麾下趙修羅所殺，北邊遂安。

translations.literal: After more than a month Shimo led his followers in surrender; Baoning again fled to the Khitan and was killed by his subordinate Zhao Xiuluo, and the northern frontier was secure.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month Shimo led his followers in surrender; Baoning fled again to the Khitan and was killed by his subordinate Zhao Xiuluo, and the northern frontier was secure.

sentences.zh: 賜物千段。

translations.literal: He was given a thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官，贈司空。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office and was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子世師嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shishi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shishi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 子世師世師少有節概，性忠厚，多武藝。

translations.literal: His son Shishi from youth had integrity and spirit, was by nature loyal and generous, and possessed many martial skills.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shishi, from youth, possessed integrity and spirit; he was loyal and generous by nature and skilled in many martial arts.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，以功臣子拜儀同，累遷驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: At weak crown, as son of a meritorious minister he was appointed Companion of the Heir and rose through posts to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of twenty, as the son of a meritorious minister, he was appointed Companion of the Heir and rose in turn to General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，領東都瓦工監。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he headed the Eastern Capital Tileworks Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Shishi headed the Eastern Capital Tileworks Directorate.

sentences.zh: 後三歲，拜張掖太守。

translations.literal: Three years later he was appointed Governor of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was appointed Governor of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐谷渾及党項羌屢為侵掠，世師至郡，有來寇者，親自捕擊，輒擒斬之，深為戎狄所憚。

translations.literal: Before this, Tuyuhun and the Qiang of Dangxiang had repeatedly raided; when Shishi reached the commandery, whenever raiders came he personally pursued and struck them, always capturing and beheading them, and the barbarians deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Tuyuhun and the Dangxiang Qiang had repeatedly raided the frontier; when Shishi reached the commandery, he personally pursued any raiders who came, capturing and beheading them on the spot, and the non-Chinese peoples came to fear him deeply.

sentences.zh: 入為武賁郎將。

translations.literal: He entered service as Valiant Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Valiant Guard General.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，出襄平道。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he marched out by the Xiangping route.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he marched out by the Xiangping route.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復擊高麗，以本官為涿郡留守。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor again attacked Goguryeo and appointed him with his existing rank as garrison commander of Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor again attacked Goguryeo and appointed him, in his existing office, garrison commander of Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 于時盜賊蜂起，世師逐捕之，往往克捷。

translations.literal: At that time bandits swarmed forth; Shishi pursued and captured them and often achieved success.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits were rising everywhere; Shishi pursued and captured them and often succeeded.

sentences.zh: 及帝還，大加賞勞，拜樓煩太守。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned he greatly rewarded and comforted him and appointed him Governor of Loufan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, he richly rewarded Shishi and appointed him Governor of Loufan.

sentences.zh: 時帝在汾陽宮，世師聞始畢可汗將為寇，勸帝幸太原。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was at Fenyang Palace; Shishi heard that Shibi Khan of the Turks was about to raid and urged the emperor to go to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was at Fenyang Palace; hearing that Shibi Khan of the Turks was about to raid, Shishi urged the emperor to withdraw to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，遂有雁門之難。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow the advice, and thus came the disaster at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him, and the disaster at Yanmen followed.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左翊衛將軍，與代王留守京師。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General of the Left Wing Guard and, with the Prince of Dai, remained to garrison the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to General of the Left Wing Guard and remained in the capital with the Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 及義軍至，世師自以世荷隋恩，又籓邸之舊，遂勒兵拒守。

translations.literal: When the righteous army arrived, Shishi considered that his family had received Sui grace for generations and that he was also an old associate of the princely residence, and therefore marshaled troops to resist and hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel army arrived, Shishi felt that his family had owed the Sui a debt across generations and that he was also an old associate of the princely household; he therefore marshaled troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 月餘，城陷，與京兆郡丞骨儀等見誅，時年五十三。

translations.literal: After more than a month the city fell; he and Jingzhao Assistant Governor Gu Yi and others were executed, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the city fell; he and Jingzhao Assistant Governor Gu Yi and others were put to death, at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 骨儀骨儀，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Gu Yi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yi came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 性剛鯁，有不可奪之志。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and unyielding, with a will that could not be taken away.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and unyielding by nature, with a will that could not be bent.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，為侍御史，處法平當，不為勢利所回。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he served as Attending Censor, applied the law fairly and appropriately, and was not turned aside by power or profit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang reign he served as Attending Censor, applied the law fairly, and would not be swayed by power or profit.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，遷尚書右司郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was moved to Right Bureau Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, he was transferred to Right Bureau Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 于時朝政漸亂濁，貨賂公行，凡當樞要之職，無問貴賤，並家累金寶。

translations.literal: At that time court government grew daily chaotic and murky; bribes were openly practiced; all who held pivotal posts, without distinction of noble or base, alike piled up gold and jewels in their households.
translations.idiomatic: At that time court government grew increasingly corrupt; bribery was practiced openly, and everyone who held a pivotal post, high or low alike, amassed gold and jewels at home.

sentences.zh: 天下士大夫莫不變節，而儀勵志守常，介然獨立。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials throughout the realm none failed to change their standards, yet Yi urged his will and held to constancy, standing alone with integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials throughout the realm changed their standards, but Yi held firm to his principles and stood alone in his integrity.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其清苦，超拜京兆郡丞，公方彌著。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his purity and hardship and promoted him beyond regular rank to Assistant Governor of Jingzhao; his public rectitude became still more evident.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his austerity and promoted him beyond the usual sequence to Assistant Governor of Jingzhao, where his public rectitude became still more evident.

sentences.zh: 時刑部尚書衛玄兼領京兆內史，頗行詭道，輒為儀所執正。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Justice Wei Xuan also held the post of Jingzhao Inner Governor and often practiced devious ways, which Yi repeatedly corrected and held to the straight.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Minister of Justice Wei Xuan also served as Jingzhao Inner Governor and often practiced devious methods, which Yi repeatedly corrected and held to account.

sentences.zh: 玄雖不便之，不能傷也。

translations.literal: Though Xuan was displeased, he could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xuan was displeased, he could not harm Yi.

sentences.zh: 及義兵至，而玄恐禍及己，遂稱老病，無所干預。

translations.literal: When the righteous army arrived, Xuan feared disaster would reach him and therefore claimed old age and illness, intervening in nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel army arrived, Xuan feared disaster would reach him and claimed old age and illness, intervening in nothing.

sentences.zh: 儀與世師同心協契，父子並誅，其後遂絕。

translations.literal: Yi and Shishi were of one heart and covenant; father and son were both executed, and thereafter the line was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Shishi stood together in loyalty; father and son were both executed, and the line was cut off.

sentences.zh: 世師有子弘智等，以年幼獲全。

translations.literal: Shishi had sons Hongzhi and others who, because they were young, were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shishi had sons Hongzhi and others who, because they were young, were spared.

sentences.zh: 竇榮定竇榮定，扶風平陵人也。

translations.literal: Dou Rongding was a native of Pingling in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Rongding came from Pingling in Fufeng commandery.

sentences.zh: 父善，周太僕。

translations.literal: His father Shan was Grand Master of the Stud under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shan had served as Grand Master of the Stud under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 季父熾，開皇初，為太傅。

translations.literal: His younger uncle Chi, at the beginning of Kaihuang, was Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Chi served as Grand Tutor at the beginning of the Kaihuang reign.

sentences.zh: 榮定沈深有器局，容貌瑰偉，美須髯，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Rongding was deep and weighty with capacity and vision; his appearance was magnificent and grand, his beard and whiskers beautiful, and he was skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Rongding was deep and weighty in bearing, with real capacity and vision; he was magnificent in appearance, with a fine beard, and skilled in archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝時，為千牛備身。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wen of Wei he served as Palace Guard of the Thousand Oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Wei he served as Palace Guard of the Thousand Oxen.

sentences.zh: 周太祖見而奇之，授平東將軍，賜爵宜君縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder saw him and marveled; he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and granted the title Viscount of Yijun County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai saw him and was impressed; he appointed him General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Yijun, with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後從太祖與齊人戰於北芒，周師不利，榮定與汝南公宇文神慶帥精騎二千邀擊之，齊師乃卻。

translations.literal: Later he followed the founder in battle with the Qi at Beimang; the Zhou army fared ill, but Rongding and the Duke of Runan Yuwen Shenqing led two thousand elite cavalry to intercept them, and the Qi army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Yuwen Tai in battle with the Qi at Beimang; the Zhou army was faring badly when Rongding and the Duke of Runan, Yuwen Shenqing, led two thousand elite cavalry in an intercepting attack, and the Qi army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以功拜上儀同。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Senior Companion of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed Senior Companion of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 後從武元皇帝引突厥木杆侵齊之并州，賜物三百段。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Wu Yuan in leading the Turk Muqan to invade Qi's Bingzhou and was given three hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Wu Yuan in leading the Turk Muqan to invade Qi's Bingzhou and was granted three hundred lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 襲爵永富縣公，邑千戶，進位開府，除忠州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Yongfu County with a fief of a thousand households, was advanced to open mansion, and was appointed Governor of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Duke of Yongfu, with a fief of a thousand households, was promoted to Open Mansion, and was appointed Governor of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，加上開府，拜前將軍、佽飛中大夫。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, he was given supernumerary open mansion and appointed Forward General and Central Grand Master of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi, he was given supernumerary Open Mansion and appointed Forward General and Central Grand Master of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 其妻則高祖姊安成長公主也。

translations.literal: His wife was the elder sister of the Grand Duke, the Princess of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Yang Jian's elder sister, the Princess of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖少小與之情契甚厚，榮定亦知高祖有人君之表，尤相推結。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke from youth shared with him a bond very deep; Rongding also knew the Grand Duke bore the marks of a ruler and especially drew close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian had been close to him from youth; Rongding also recognized in him the marks of a ruler and drew especially close to him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖作相，領左右宮伯，使鎮守天臺，總統露門內兩箱仗衛，常宿禁中。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke became chancellor he headed the Left and Right Palace Chiefs, was sent to garrison Tiantai, commanded the two wings of armed guards within the Dew Gate, and regularly lodged in the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became chancellor, Rongding headed the Left and Right Palace Chiefs, was sent to garrison Tiantai, commanded the two wings of armed guards within the Dew Gate, and regularly lodged in the palace.

sentences.zh: 遇尉迥初平，朝廷頗以山東為意，乃拜榮定為洛州總管以鎮之。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Yong had just been pacified, the court was much concerned about the eastern mountains and therefore appointed Rongding overall commander of Luozhou to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Yong had just been pacified, the court was much concerned about the eastern provinces and appointed Rongding overall commander of Luozhou to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 前後賜縑四千匹，西涼女樂一部。

translations.literal: Before and after he was given four thousand bolts of thin silk and one troupe of Xiliang female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after he was granted four thousand bolts of thin silk and a troupe of Xiliang female musicians.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，來朝京師。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke received the abdication he came to court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Rongding came to court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 上顧謂群臣曰：「朕少惡輕薄，性相近者，唯竇榮定而已。

translations.literal: The emperor turned and said to the assembled ministers: "From youth I have detested the frivolous; of those whose natures are close to mine, there is only Dou Rongding."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to the assembled ministers and said, "From youth I have detested the frivolous; of those whose nature is close to mine, there is only Dou Rongding."

sentences.zh: 」賜馬三百匹，部曲八十戶而遣之。

translations.literal: He was given three hundred horses and eighty households of retainers and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three hundred horses and eighty households of retainers and sent back.

sentences.zh: 坐事除名，高祖以長公主之故，尋拜右武候大將軍。

translations.literal: He was struck from the rolls on account of an offense, but because of the Princess of Ancheng the Grand Duke soon appointed him General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was struck from the rolls on account of an offense, but because of the Princess of Ancheng, Yang Jian soon appointed him General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 上數幸其第，恩賜甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor often visited his residence and his favors and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited his residence, and his favors and gifts were very generous.

sentences.zh: 每令尚食局日供羊一口，珍味稱是。

translations.literal: He regularly ordered the Imperial Kitchen Bureau to supply one sheep per day, with delicacies to match.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly ordered the Imperial Kitchen Bureau to supply one sheep per day, with delicacies to match.

sentences.zh: 以佐命功，拜上柱國、甯州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit in assisting the mandate he was appointed Senior Pillar of State and Governor of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in assisting the founding of the dynasty, he was appointed Senior Pillar of State and Governor of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為右武候大將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he again became General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again became General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋除秦州總管，賜吳樂一部。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed overall commander of Qinzhou and given one troupe of Wu music.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed overall commander of Qinzhou and granted a troupe of Wu music.

sentences.zh: 突厥沙缽略寇邊，以為行軍元帥，率九總管，步騎三萬，出涼州。

translations.literal: When the Turk Shabolue raided the frontier, he was made marching supreme commander, leading nine overall commanders and thirty thousand foot and horse, marching out from Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turk Shabolue raided the frontier, he was made marching supreme commander, leading nine overall commanders and thirty thousand infantry and cavalry out from Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 與虜戰于高越原，兩軍相持，其地無水，士卒渴甚，至刺馬血而飲，死者十有二三。

translations.literal: He fought the barbarians at Gaoyue Plain; the two armies faced each other, the place had no water, the soldiers were desperately thirsty, and they went so far as to pierce horse blood to drink; one or two in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the enemy at Gaoyue Plain; the two armies faced each other in a place without water, and the soldiers grew desperately thirsty, going so far as to pierce their horses and drink the blood; one or two soldiers in ten died.

sentences.zh: 榮定仰天太息。

translations.literal: Rongding looked up to Heaven and sighed deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Rongding looked up to Heaven and sighed deeply.

sentences.zh: 俄而澍雨，軍乃復振。

translations.literal: Soon a timely rain fell and the army was restored to vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a timely rain fell, and the army recovered its strength.

sentences.zh: 於是進擊，數挫其鋒，突厥憚之，請盟而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced in attack, repeatedly blunted their edge, the Turks feared him, and they requested alliance and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced in attack, repeatedly blunted their momentum, and the Turks, fearing him, sought peace and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賜縑萬匹，進爵安豐郡公，增邑千六百戶。

translations.literal: He was given ten thousand bolts of thin silk, advanced in rank to Duke of Anfeng commandery, and his fief increased by sixteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted ten thousand bolts of thin silk, advanced to Duke of Anfeng, and his fief increased by sixteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 復封子憲為安康郡公，賜縑五千匹。

translations.literal: His son Xian was again enfeoffed as Duke of Ankang commandery and given five thousand bolts of thin silk.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian was enfeoffed as Duke of Ankang and granted five thousand bolts of thin silk.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜右武衛大將軍，俄轉左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed General of the Right Martial Guard and soon transferred to General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed General of the Right Martial Guard and soon transferred to General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 上欲以為三公，榮定上書曰：「臣每觀西朝衛、霍，東都梁、鄧，幸托葭莩，位極台鉉，寵積驕盈，必致傾覆。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make him one of the Three Dukes; Rongding submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has often observed the Western Han's Wei and Huo, the Eastern Capital's Liang and Deng—fortunate in kinship by marriage, their posts reaching the highest offices, favor piled up until pride overflowed, and inevitably they came to overturn."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint him one of the Three Dukes; Rongding submitted a memorial saying, "I have often observed the Western Han's Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, and the Eastern Han's Liang Ji and Deng Zhi—men who, through marriage ties to the throne, rose to the highest offices, accumulated favor until pride overflowed, and inevitably brought ruin upon themselves."

sentences.zh: 向使前賢，少自貶損，遠避權勢，推而不居，則天命可保，何覆宗之有！

translations.literal: If only the former worthies had modestly lowered themselves, kept far from power and influence, and pushed forward without occupying the post, then the mandate of Heaven could have been preserved—how could there have been the overturning of their clans!
translations.idiomatic: Had those former worthies humbled themselves a little, kept far from power, and declined what was offered them, the mandate of Heaven could have been preserved—how could their clans have been destroyed!

sentences.zh: 臣每覽前修，實為畏懼。

translations.literal: Your subject, whenever he reads of former exemplars, truly feels fear and dread.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read of those former exemplars, I am truly filled with fear.

sentences.zh: 」上於是乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after could not be fully counted.
translations.idiomatic: The rewards granted him before and after cannot be fully counted.

sentences.zh: 開皇六年卒，時年五十七。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Kaihuang, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Kaihuang, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 上為之廢朝，令左衛大將軍元旻監護喪事，賻縑三千匹。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court for him, ordered Left Guard General Yuan Min to oversee the funeral, and gave three thousand bolts of thin silk as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court for him, ordered Left Guard General Yuan Min to oversee the funeral, and granted three thousand bolts of thin silk as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「吾每欲致榮定於三事，其人固讓不可。

translations.literal: The emperor told the attending ministers: "I have often wished to elevate Rongding to the Three Offices, but the man firmly declined and it could not be done."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told those attending him, "I have often wished to elevate Rongding to the Three Offices, but he firmly declined and would not accept."

sentences.zh: 今欲贈之，重違其志。

translations.literal: Now I wish to grant him posthumous honors, yet that would again violate his will.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to grant him posthumous honors, yet that would again violate his will.

sentences.zh: 」於是贈冀州刺史、陳國公，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He was therefore posthumously made Governor of Jizhou and Duke of Chen state, with the posthumous name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore posthumously appointed Governor of Jizhou and Duke of Chen, with the posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 子抗嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 抗美容儀，性通率，長於巧思。

translations.literal: Kang had a beautiful bearing, was by nature frank and direct, and excelled in ingenious thought.
translations.idiomatic: Kang had a handsome bearing, was frank and direct by nature, and excelled in ingenious invention.

sentences.zh: 父卒之後，恩遇彌隆，所賜錢帛金寶，亦以巨萬。

translations.literal: After his father's death his favor grew still greater, and the money, silks, gold, and jewels granted him also reached the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death his favor grew still greater, and the money, silks, gold, and jewels granted him also reached into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 抗官至定州刺史，復檢校幽州總管。

translations.literal: Kang reached the post of Governor of Dingzhou and was again made acting overall commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kang rose to Governor of Dingzhou and was also made acting overall commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，漢王諒構逆，以為抗與通謀，由是除名，以其弟慶襲封陳公焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, the Prince of Han, Liang, rose in rebellion; Kang was thought to have conspired with him and was therefore struck from the rolls, and his younger brother Qing inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, the Prince of Han, Liang, rose in rebellion; Kang was thought to have conspired with him and was struck from the rolls, and his younger brother Qing inherited the title of Duke of Chen.

sentences.zh: 慶亦有姿儀，性和厚，頗工草隸。

translations.literal: Qing also had a fine bearing, was by nature mild and generous, and was quite skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Qing also had a fine bearing, was mild and generous by nature, and was quite skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 初封永富郡公，官至河東太守、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Yongfu commandery and reached the posts of Governor of Hedong and Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Yongfu and rose to Governor of Hedong and Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 大業之末，出為南郡太守，為盜賊所害。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he went out as Governor of Nan commandery and was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign he was sent out as Governor of Nan commandery and was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 慶弟璿，亦工草隸，頗解鐘律。

translations.literal: Qing's younger brother Xuan was also skilled in cursive and clerical script and understood bell-tones and pitch pipes quite well.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's younger brother Xuan was also skilled in cursive and clerical script and understood music theory quite well.

sentences.zh: 官曆潁川、南郡、扶風太守。

translations.literal: In office he served in succession as Governor of Yingchuan, Nan, and Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Governor of Yingchuan, Nan, and Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 元景山元景山，字珤岳，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Jingshan, styled Baoyue, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jingshan, whose courtesy name was Baoyue, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖燮，魏安定王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xie was Prince of Anding under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xie was Prince of Anding under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父琰，宋安王。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Prince of Song'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan was Prince of Song'an.

sentences.zh: 景山少有器局，幹略過人。

translations.literal: Jingshan from youth had capacity and vision, his strategic ability surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jingshan possessed capacity and vision, with strategic ability surpassing others.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝時，從大司馬賀蘭祥擊吐谷渾，以功拜撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Min of Zhou he followed Grand Marshal Helan Xiang in attacking Tuyuhun and for merit was appointed Pacifying Army General.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Min of Zhou he followed Grand Marshal Helan Xiang in an attack on Tuyuhun and, for his merit, was appointed Pacifying Army General.

sentences.zh: 其後數從征伐，累遷儀同三司，賜爵文昌縣公，授亹川防主。

translations.literal: Thereafter he repeatedly followed on campaigns, rose through posts to Companion of the Heir, Third Rank, was granted the title Duke of Wenchang County, and was appointed Defender of Weichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he took part in many campaigns, rose in turn to Companion of the Heir, Third Rank, was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenchang, and was appointed Defender of Weichuan.

sentences.zh: 後與齊人戰於北邙，斬級居多，加開府，遷建州刺史，進封宋安郡公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: Later he fought the Qi at Beimang, beheaded the most enemy heads, was given open mansion, was moved to Governor of Jianzhou, and was advanced to Duke of Song'an commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fought the Qi at Beimang, took the most enemy heads, was given Open Mansion, was transferred to Governor of Jianzhou, and was advanced to Duke of Song'an with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，每戰有功，拜大將軍，改封平原郡公，邑二千戶，賜女樂一部，帛六千匹，奴婢二百五十口，牛羊數千。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, in every battle he had merit; he was appointed Great General, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan commandery with a fief of two thousand households, and given one troupe of female musicians, six thousand bolts of silk, two hundred fifty bondsmen and bondswomen, and several thousand cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi, he distinguished himself in every battle; he was appointed Great General, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan with a fief of two thousand households, and granted a troupe of female musicians, six thousand bolts of silk, two hundred fifty bondsmen and bondswomen, and several thousand cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 治亳州總管。

translations.literal: He governed as overall commander of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as overall commander of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，州民王回洛、張季真等聚結亡命，每為劫盜。

translations.literal: Before this, subjects Wang Huiluo, Zhang Jizhen, and others gathered fugitives and outlaws and repeatedly committed robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, local men Wang Huiluo, Zhang Jizhen, and others had gathered fugitives and outlaws and repeatedly committed robbery.

sentences.zh: 前後牧守不能制。

translations.literal: Governors before and after could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Successive governors had been unable to control them.

sentences.zh: 景山下車，逐捕之，回洛、季真挺身奔江南。

translations.literal: When Jingshan descended from his carriage he pursued and captured them; Huiluo and Jizhen fled in person to the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingshan took up his post he pursued and captured them; Huiluo and Jizhen fled in person to the south.

sentences.zh: 禽其黨與數百人，皆斬之。

translations.literal: He captured several hundred of their associates and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: He captured several hundred of their associates and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 法令明肅，盜賊屏跡，稱為大治。

translations.literal: Laws and orders were clear and stern, bandits vanished from sight, and the region was called greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: With laws clear and stern, bandits vanished from sight, and the region was said to be greatly well governed.

sentences.zh: 陳人張景遵以淮南內屬，為陳將任蠻奴所攻，破其數柵。

translations.literal: The Chen subject Zhang Jingzun submitted Huainan to allegiance within the realm and was attacked by the Chen general Ren Mannu, who broke several of his stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingzun of Chen submitted Huainan to allegiance within the realm and was attacked by the Chen general Ren Mannu, who broke several of his stockades.

sentences.zh: 景山發譙、潁兵援之，蠻奴引軍而退。

translations.literal: Jingshan sent troops from Qiao and Ying to aid him, and Mannu withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan sent troops from Qiao and Ying to aid him, and Mannu withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 徵為候正。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Rectifier of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Rectifier of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，從上柱國韋孝寬經略淮南。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded he followed Senior Pillar of State Wei Xiaokuan in planning Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he followed Senior Pillar of State Wei Xiaokuan in the campaign in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 鄖州總管宇文亮謀圖不軌，以輕兵襲孝寬。

translations.literal: Yunzhou overall commander Yuwen Liang plotted an improper course and struck Xiaokuan with light troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhou overall commander Yuwen Liang plotted rebellion and struck Xiaokuan with light troops.

sentences.zh: 孝寬窘迫，未得整陣，為亮所薄。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was hard pressed and had not been able to form his battle line; he was pressed by Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan was hard pressed and had not been able to form his battle line; Liang pressed him hard.

sentences.zh: 景山率鐵騎三百出擊，破之，斬亮傳首。

translations.literal: Jingshan led three hundred iron cavalry out in attack, defeated him, beheaded Liang, and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan led three hundred armored cavalry out in attack, defeated him, beheaded Liang, and sent his head.

sentences.zh: 以功拜亳州總管。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed overall commander of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed overall commander of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥稱兵作亂。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke was chancellor, Yuwen Yong raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chancellor, Yuwen Yong raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 滎州刺史宇文胄與迥通謀，陰以書諷動景山。

translations.literal: Xingyang Governor Yuwen Zhou conspired with Yong and secretly sent a letter to urge and move Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyang Governor Yuwen Zhou conspired with Yong and secretly sent a letter urging Jingshan to join them.

sentences.zh: 景山執其使，封書詣相府。

translations.literal: Jingshan seized his envoy, sealed the letter, and went to the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan seized the envoy, sealed the letter, and took it to the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚嘉之，進位上大將軍。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke greatly praised him and advanced him to Senior Great General.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian greatly praised him and promoted him to Senior Great General.

sentences.zh: 司馬消難之以鄖州入陳也，陳遣將樊毅、馬傑等來援。

translations.literal: When Sima Xiaonan submitted Yunzhou to Chen, Chen sent generals Fan Yi, Ma Jie, and others to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiaonan submitted Yunzhou to Chen, Chen sent generals Fan Yi, Ma Jie, and others to aid him.

sentences.zh: 景山率輕騎五百馳赴之。

translations.literal: Jingshan led five hundred light cavalry in rapid advance to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan led five hundred light cavalry in rapid advance to meet them.

sentences.zh: 毅等懼，掠居民而遁。

translations.literal: Yi and the others were afraid, plundered the residents, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others were afraid, plundered the local people, and fled.

sentences.zh: 景山追之，一日一夜行三百餘里，與毅戰於漳口，二合皆克。

translations.literal: Jingshan pursued them, traveling more than three hundred li in one day and one night, fought Yi at Zhangkou, and in two engagements both were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan pursued them, traveling more than three hundred li in a day and a night, fought Yi at Zhangkou, and won both engagements.

sentences.zh: 毅等退保甑山鎮。

translations.literal: Yi and the others withdrew to hold Zengshan town.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others withdrew to hold Zengshan town.

sentences.zh: 其城邑為消難所陷者，悉平之。

translations.literal: The cities and towns that Xiaonan had taken were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The cities and towns that Xiaonan had taken were all recovered.

sentences.zh: 拜安州總管，進位柱國，前後賜帛二千匹。

translations.literal: He was appointed overall commander of Anzhou, advanced to Pillar of State, and before and after was given two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed overall commander of Anzhou, promoted to Pillar of State, and granted two thousand bolts of silk in all.

sentences.zh: 時桐柏山蠻相聚為亂，景山復擊平之。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarians of Tongbai Mountain gathered together in rebellion; Jingshan again attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the tribes of Tongbai Mountain gathered in rebellion; Jingshan attacked again and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜上柱國。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke received the abdication he was appointed Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Jingshan was appointed Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 明年，大舉伐陳，以景山為行軍元帥，率行軍總管韓延、呂哲出漢口。

translations.literal: The next year a great campaign was launched against Chen; Jingshan was made marching supreme commander, leading marching commanders-in-chief Han Yan and Lü Zhe out from Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year a great campaign was launched against Chen; Jingshan was made marching supreme commander and led marching commanders-in-chief Han Yan and Lü Zhe out from Hankou.

sentences.zh: 遣上開府鄧孝儒將勁卒四千，攻陳甑山鎮。

translations.literal: He sent supernumerary open-mansion holder Deng Xiaoru leading four thousand crack troops to attack Chen's Zengshan town.
translations.idiomatic: He sent supernumerary Open Mansion holder Deng Xiaoru at the head of four thousand crack troops to attack Chen's Zengshan town.

sentences.zh: 陳人遣其將陸綸以舟師來援。

translations.literal: The Chen sent their general Lu Lun with a fleet to aid the town.
translations.idiomatic: Chen sent their general Lu Lun with a fleet to aid the town.

sentences.zh: 孝儒逆擊，破之。

translations.literal: Xiaoru met them in counterattack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru met them in counterattack and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 陳將魯達、陳紀以兵守溳口，景山復遣兵擊走之。

translations.literal: The Chen generals Lu Da and Chen Ji held Yunkou with troops; Jingshan again sent troops to attack and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen generals Lu Da and Chen Ji held Yunkou with troops; Jingshan again sent troops to attack and drive them off.

sentences.zh: 陳人大駭，甑山、沌陽二鎮守將皆棄城而遁。

translations.literal: The Chen were greatly alarmed; the garrison commanders of Zengshan and Dunyang towns both abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen were greatly alarmed; the garrison commanders of Zengshan and Dunyang both abandoned their towns and fled.

sentences.zh: 景山將濟江，會陳宣帝卒，有詔班師。

translations.literal: Jingshan was about to cross the Yangzi when Emperor Xuan of Chen died and an edict ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan was about to cross the Yangzi when Emperor Xuan of Chen died and an edict ordered the army to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 景山大著威名，甚為敵人所憚。

translations.literal: Jingshan greatly established his reputation for might and was deeply feared by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan's reputation for might grew greatly, and the enemy feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 後數載，坐事免，卒於家。

translations.literal: Several years later he was dismissed on account of an offense and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was dismissed on account of an offense and died at home.

sentences.zh: 時年五十五。

translations.literal: He was aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 贈梁州總管，賜縑千匹，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made overall commander of Liangzhou, given a thousand bolts of thin silk, and given the posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed overall commander of Liangzhou, granted a thousand bolts of thin silk, and given the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子成壽嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chengshou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengshou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 成壽便弓馬，起家千牛備身。

translations.literal: Chengshou was skilled at bow and horse and began his career as Palace Guard of the Thousand Oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshou was skilled in archery and horsemanship and entered service as Palace Guard of the Thousand Oxen.

sentences.zh: 以上柱國世子，拜儀同。

translations.literal: As heir of a Senior Pillar of State he was appointed Companion of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a Senior Pillar of State he was appointed Companion of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 後為秦王庫真車騎。

translations.literal: Later he served as Chariots and Cavalry of the Prince of Qin's household guard.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Chariots and Cavalry in the household guard of the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，徵為左親衛郎將。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as General of the Left Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, he was summoned to serve as General of the Left Personal Guard.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之亂也，從刑部尚書衛玄擊之，以功進位正議大夫，拜西平通守。

translations.literal: In Yang Xuangan's rebellion he followed Minister of Justice Wei Xuan in attacking him; for merit he was advanced to Rectifying Counselor and appointed Transit Governor of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: During Yang Xuangan's rebellion he followed Minister of Justice Wei Xuan in attacking the rebels; for his merit he was promoted to Rectifying Counselor and appointed Transit Governor of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 源雄源雄，字世略，西平樂都人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiong, styled Shilüe, was a native of Ledu in Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiong, whose courtesy name was Shilüe, came from Ledu in Xiping.

sentences.zh: 祖懷、父纂，俱為魏隴西王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huai and father Zuan were both Princes of Longxi under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huai and father Zuan had both been Princes of Longxi under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 雄少寬厚，偉姿儀。

translations.literal: Xiong from youth was generous and magnanimous, with a magnificent bearing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiong was generous and magnanimous, with a magnificent bearing.

sentences.zh: 在魏起家秘書郎，尋加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Under Wei he began his career as Secretariat Gentleman and soon was additionally made General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei he entered service as Secretariat Gentleman and was soon additionally appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 屬其父為高氏所誅，雄脫身而遁，變姓名，西歸長安。

translations.literal: When his father was executed by the Gao clan, Xiong escaped and fled, changed his name, and returned west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was executed by the Gao clan, Xiong escaped, changed his name, and fled west to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 周太祖見而器之，賜爵隴西郡公。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder saw him and valued him, granting him the title Duke of Longxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai saw him and valued him, enfeoffing him as Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 後從武帝伐齊，以功授開府，改封朔方郡公，拜冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Wu in campaigning against Qi; for merit he was given open mansion, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shuofang commandery, and appointed Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Wu in the campaign against Qi; for his merit he was given Open Mansion, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shuofang, and appointed Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 時以突厥寇邊，徙雄為平州刺史以鎮之。

translations.literal: At that time because the Turks raided the frontier, Xiong was moved to Governor of Pingzhou to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, because the Turks were raiding the frontier, Xiong was transferred to Governor of Pingzhou to garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校徐州總管。

translations.literal: Before long he was made acting overall commander of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting overall commander of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂，時雄家累在相州，迥潛以書誘之，雄卒不顧。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke was chancellor, Yuwen Yong rose in rebellion; at that time Xiong's family dependents were in Xiangzhou, and Yong secretly sent a letter to entice him, but Xiong in the end paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chancellor, Yuwen Yong rose in rebellion; at that time Xiong's family was in Xiangzhou, and Yong secretly sent a letter to entice him, but Xiong paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 高祖遺雄書曰：「公妻子在鄴城，雖言離隔，賊徒翦滅，聚會非難。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke sent Xiong a letter saying: "Your wife and children are in Yecheng; though one speaks of separation, once the rebel band is cut down, reunion will not be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian sent Xiong a letter saying, "Your wife and children are in Yecheng; though you are separated now, once the rebels are destroyed, reunion will not be difficult."

sentences.zh: 今日已後，不過數旬之別，遲能開慰，無以累懷。

translations.literal: From today onward it is no more than a separation of several tens of days; you will soon be able to open your heart in comfort—do not let it burden your thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: From today onward it is only a separation of several tens of days; you will soon be reunited—do not let it weigh on your mind.

sentences.zh: 徐部大蕃，東南襟帶，密邇吳寇，特須安撫。

translations.literal: Xuzhou is a great flourishing region, the girdle and belt of the southeast, close to the Wu raiders and especially in need of comforting settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou is a great and flourishing region, the strategic belt of the southeast, close to the Wu enemy and especially in need of pacification.

sentences.zh: 藉公英略，委以邊謀，善建功名，用副朝委也。

translations.literal: Relying on your public strategic ability, I entrust you with frontier planning; build merit and fame well and thereby fulfill the court's commission.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on your strategic ability, I entrust you with frontier affairs; build merit and fame and fulfill the court's commission.

sentences.zh: 」迥遣其將畢義緒據蘭陵，席毗陷昌慮、下邑。

translations.literal: Yong sent his general Bi Yixu to hold Lanling; Xi Pi took Changlu and Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent his general Bi Yixu to hold Lanling; Xi Pi took Changlu and Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 雄遣徐州刺史劉仁恩擊義緒，儀同劉弘、李琰討席毗，悉平之。

translations.literal: Xiong sent Xuzhou Governor Liu Ren'en to attack Yixu and Companions of the Heir Liu Hong and Li Yan to campaign against Xi Pi; all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong sent Xuzhou Governor Liu Ren'en to attack Yixu and Companions of the Heir Liu Hong and Li Yan to campaign against Xi Pi; all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 陳人見中原多故，遣其將陳紀、蕭摩訶、任蠻奴、周羅睺、樊毅等侵江北，西自江陵，東距壽陽，民多應之，攻陷城鎮。

translations.literal: The Chen, seeing many troubles in the central plains, sent their generals Chen Ji, Xiao Mohe, Ren Mannu, Zhou Luohou, Fan Yi, and others to invade north of the Yangzi; west from Jiangling to east as far as Shouyang, many people responded and they attacked and took cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing many troubles in the central plains, Chen sent generals Chen Ji, Xiao Mohe, Ren Mannu, Zhou Luohou, Fan Yi, and others to invade the north bank of the Yangzi; from Jiangling in the west to Shouyang in the east, many people joined them and they captured cities and towns.

sentences.zh: 雄與吳州總管于顗、揚州總管賀若弼、黃州總管元景山等擊走之，悉復故地。

translations.literal: Xiong with Wuzhou overall commander Yu Kai, Yangzhou overall commander He Ruo Bi, Huangzhou overall commander Yuan Jingshan, and others attacked and drove them off, fully recovering the former territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, together with Wuzhou overall commander Yu Kai, Yangzhou overall commander He Ruo Bi, Huangzhou overall commander Yuan Jingshan, and others, attacked and drove them off, fully recovering the former territory.

sentences.zh: 東潼州刺史曹孝達據州作亂，雄遣兵襲斬之。

translations.literal: Eastern Tongzhou Governor Cao Xiaoda held the province in rebellion; Xiong sent troops to strike and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Tongzhou Governor Cao Xiaoda held the province in rebellion; Xiong sent troops to strike and behead him.

sentences.zh: 進位上大將軍，拜徐州總管。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Senior Great General and appointed overall commander of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Senior Great General and appointed overall commander of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，轉懷州刺史，尋遷朔州總管。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to Governor of Huaizhou and soon moved to overall commander of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to Governor of Huaizhou and soon moved to overall commander of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥有來寇掠，雄輒捕斬之，深為北夷所憚。

translations.literal: Whenever Turks came to raid and plunder, Xiong would capture and behead them, and the northern barbarians deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Turks came to raid, Xiong would capture and behead them, and the northern peoples deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，高祖下冊書曰：「於戲！

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen the Grand Duke issued a patent of appointment saying: "Alas!"
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen, the emperor issued a patent of appointment that read, "Alas!"

sentences.zh: 唯爾上大將軍、朔方公雄，識悟明允，風神果毅。

translations.literal: Only you, Senior Great General and Duke of Shuofang Xiong, are perceptive, enlightened, clear, and fair, with spirit and bearing decisive and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Only you, Senior Great General and Duke of Shuofang Xiong, are perceptive and fair, with a spirit decisive and resolute.

sentences.zh: 往牧徐方，時逢寇逆，建旟馬邑，安撫北蕃。

translations.literal: Formerly governing Xuzhou, you met rebel invaders; you raised banners at Mayi and comforted the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly governing Xuzhou, you met rebel invaders; you raised your banners at Mayi and pacified the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 嘉謀絕外境之虞，挺劍息韋韝之望。

translations.literal: Your excellent plans cut off anxieties beyond the borders; you drew your sword and quieted the hopes of the leather-bowed.
