translations.idiomatic: Your excellent plans cut off threats beyond the borders; you drew your sword and quieted the ambitions of the bow-bearing peoples.

sentences.zh: 沙漠以北，俱荷威恩，呂梁之間，罔不懷惠。

translations.literal: North of the desert all bore your authority and grace; between the Lüliang ranges none failed to cherish your kindness.
translations.idiomatic: North of the desert all bore your authority and grace; throughout the Lüliang region none failed to cherish your kindness.

sentences.zh: 但江淮蕞爾，有陳僭逆，今將董率戎旅，清彼東南，是用命爾為行軍總管。

translations.literal: But the Yangzi and Huai are a trifling region, where Chen holds wrongful rebellion; now I shall lead the army to clear the southeast—therefore I appoint you marching commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: But the Yangzi and Huai region, though small, harbors the wrongful rebellion of Chen; now I shall lead the army to clear the southeast—therefore I appoint you marching commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉！

translations.literal: Go and take reverent heed!
translations.idiomatic: Go, and take reverent heed!

sentences.zh: 」於是從秦王俊出信州道。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed Prince Jun of Qin out by the Xinzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he followed Prince Jun of Qin out by the Xinzhou route.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，以功進位上柱國。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified he was advanced to Senior Pillar of State for merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was pacified he was promoted to Senior Pillar of State for his merit.

sentences.zh: 賜子崇爵端氏縣伯，褒為安化縣伯，賜物五千段，復鎮朔州。

translations.literal: His son Chong was granted the title Baron of Duanshi County, Bao was made Baron of Anhua County, five thousand lengths of goods were given, and he again garrisoned Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong was enfeoffed as Baron of Duanshi, Bao as Baron of Anhua, he was granted five thousand lengths of goods, and he again garrisoned Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 二歲，上表乞骸骨，征還京師，卒于家，時年七十。

translations.literal: After two years he submitted a memorial requesting to yield his bones, was summoned back to the capital, and died at home, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he submitted a memorial requesting retirement, was recalled to the capital, and died at home, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 子崇嗣，官至儀同。

translations.literal: His son Chong succeeded and reached the post of Companion of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong succeeded him and rose to Companion of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 大業中，自上黨贊治入為尚書虞部郎。

translations.literal: Under Daye he entered from Assistant Administrator of Shangdang as Director of the Parks Bureau of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Daye reign he entered service from Assistant Administrator of Shangdang as Director of the Parks Bureau of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及天下盜起，將兵討北海，與賊力戰而死，贈正議大夫。

translations.literal: When bandits rose throughout the realm he led troops to campaign against Beihai, fought the rebels bitterly, and died; he was posthumously made Rectifying Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose throughout the realm he led troops against Beihai, fought the rebels bitterly, and died; he was posthumously appointed Rectifying Counselor.

sentences.zh: 豆盧勣豆盧勣，字定東，昌黎徒河人也。

translations.literal: Dou Luji, styled Dingdong, was a native of Tuhe in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luji, whose courtesy name was Dingdong, came from Tuhe in Changli.

sentences.zh: 本姓慕容，燕北地王精之後也。

translations.literal: His original surname was Murong; he was a descendant of Jing, King of Northern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Murong; he was a descendant of Jing, King of Northern Yan.

sentences.zh: 中山敗，歸魏，北人謂歸義為「豆盧」，因氏焉。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was defeated they submitted to Wei; northerners called submission to righteousness "Dou Lu," and thus they took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshan fell they submitted to the Wei; northerners called submission to righteousness "Dou Lu," and thus they took it as their clan name.

sentences.zh: 祖萇，魏柔玄鎮大將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang was Great General of Rouxuan Garrison under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang had served as Great General of Rouxuan Garrison under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父甯，柱國、太保。

translations.literal: His father Ning was Pillar of State and Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning had been Pillar of State and Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 勣初生時，周太祖親幸甯家稱慶，時遇新破齊師，太祖因字之曰定東。

translations.literal: When Luji was first born the Zhou founder personally visited the Ning household to offer congratulations; it happened that Qi forces had just been newly defeated, and the founder therefore gave him the courtesy name Dingdong (Settling the East).
translations.idiomatic: When Luji was born, Yuwen Tai personally visited the Ning household to offer congratulations; it happened that Qi forces had just been defeated, and Yuwen Tai therefore gave him the courtesy name Dingdong (Settling the East).

sentences.zh: 勣聰悟，有器局。

translations.literal: Luji was intelligent and perceptive, with capacity and vision.
translations.idiomatic: Luji was intelligent and perceptive, with real capacity and vision.

sentences.zh: 少受業國子學，略涉文藝。

translations.literal: In youth he studied at the Imperial Academy and dipped slightly into literary arts.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied at the Imperial Academy and gained some acquaintance with literary arts.

sentences.zh: 魏大統十二年，太祖以勣勳臣子，封義安縣侯。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Datong under Wei, the founder because Luji was the son of a meritorious minister enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yi'an County.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Datong under the Wei, Yuwen Tai enfeoffed Luji as Marquis of Yi'an, as the son of a meritorious minister.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝受禪，授稍伯下大夫、開府儀同三司，改封丹陽郡公，邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Zhou received the abdication he was appointed Junior Grand Master of the Left, open mansion Companion of the Heir Third Rank, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Danyang commandery with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Zhou took the throne, he was appointed Junior Grand Master of the Left and Open Mansion Companion of the Heir, Third Rank, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Danyang with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，為左武伯中大夫。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming he was Central Grand Master of the Left Martial Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he served as Central Grand Master of the Left Martial Chief.

sentences.zh: 勣自以經業未通，請解職遊露門學。

translations.literal: Luji considered that his classical studies were not yet mastered and requested to leave office to study at the Dew Gate Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Luji considered that his classical studies were not yet complete and requested to leave office to study at the Dew Gate Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，敕以本官就學。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and ordered him to study while retaining his existing office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this and ordered him to study while retaining his existing office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，齊王憲納勣妹為妃，恩禮逾厚。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Qi, Xian, took Luji's younger sister as consort, and favor and courtesy grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Prince of Qi, Xian, took Luji's younger sister as consort, and imperial favor toward the family grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 會武帝嗣位，拜邛州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu succeeded he was appointed Governor of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu came to the throne, he was appointed Governor of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 未之官，渭源燒當羌因饑饉作亂，以勣有才略，轉渭州刺史。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, the Shao Dang Qiang of Weiyuan rose in rebellion on account of famine; because Luji had talent and strategy he was transferred to Governor of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the post, the Shao Dang Qiang of Weiyuan rose in rebellion on account of famine; because Luji had talent and strategic ability, he was transferred to Governor of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 甚有惠政，華夷悅服，德澤流行，大致祥瑞。

translations.literal: He had very benevolent government; Chinese and non-Chinese alike were pleased and submitted; his virtue and grace spread widely, and for the most part auspicious omens appeared.
translations.idiomatic: His government was deeply benevolent; Chinese and non-Chinese alike were pleased and submitted; his virtue spread widely, and auspicious omens appeared in great number.

sentences.zh: 鳥鼠山俗呼為高武隴，其下渭水所出，其山絕壁千尋，由來乏水，諸羌苦之。

translations.literal: Wushu Mountain was commonly called Gaowu Long; below it the Wei River issued forth; the mountain had sheer cliffs a thousand fathoms high, and from old times water had been scarce—the various Qiang suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: Wushu Mountain was commonly called Gaowu Long; the Wei River issued from its foot; the mountain had sheer cliffs a thousand fathoms high, and from old times water had been scarce—the Qiang peoples suffered greatly from this.

sentences.zh: 勣馬足所踐，忽飛泉湧出。

translations.literal: Where Luji's horse's hooves trod, suddenly a flying spring gushed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Where Luji's horse trod, a spring suddenly gushed forth.

sentences.zh: 有白鳥翔止廳前，乳子而後去，又白狼見於襄武。

translations.literal: A white bird flew and alighted before the hall, nursed its young, and then departed; moreover a white wolf appeared at Xiangwu.
translations.idiomatic: A white bird flew down and alighted before the hall, nursed its young, and then departed; a white wolf also appeared at Xiangwu.

sentences.zh: 民為之謠曰：「我有丹陽，山出玉漿。

translations.literal: The people made a song for him saying: "We have Danyang; the mountain yields jade broth."
translations.idiomatic: The people made a song for him that ran, "We have Danyang; the mountain yields jade broth."

sentences.zh: 濟我民夷，神鳥來翔。

translations.literal: It aids our people, Chinese and barbarian; the divine bird comes flying."
translations.idiomatic: It aids our people, Chinese and non-Chinese alike; the divine bird comes flying."

sentences.zh: 」百姓因號其泉為玉漿泉。

translations.literal: The common people therefore called the spring Jade Broth Spring.
translations.idiomatic: The people therefore called the spring Jade Broth Spring.

sentences.zh: 後丁父艱，毀瘁過禮。

translations.literal: Later he entered mourning for his father and was wasted beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later, upon his father's death, he mourned with a grief beyond what the rites required.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，授邵州刺史，襲爵楚國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe he was appointed Governor of Shaozhou and inherited the title Duke of Chu state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe he was appointed Governor of Shaozhou and inherited the title Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 復徵為天官府司會，歷信、夏二州總管、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as Director of the Celestial Offices Bureau and served in succession as overall commander of Xin and Xia provinces and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned as Director of the Celestial Offices Bureau and served in turn as overall commander of Xin and Xia provinces and as Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以母憂還京。

translations.literal: On account of mourning for his mother he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his mother's death he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 宣帝大象二年，拜利州總管，進位上大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang under Emperor Xuan he was appointed overall commander of Lizhou and advanced to Senior Great General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daxiang under Emperor Xuan he was appointed overall commander of Lizhou and promoted to Senior Great General.

sentences.zh: 月餘，拜柱國。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was appointed Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he was appointed Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，益州總管王謙作亂。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke was chancellor, Yizhou overall commander Wang Qian rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chancellor, Yizhou overall commander Wang Qian rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 勣嬰城固守，謙遣其將達奚念、高阿那肱、乙弗虔等眾十萬攻之，起土山，鑿城為七十餘穴，堰江水以灌之。

translations.literal: Luji closed the city and held firm in defense; Qian sent his generals Daxi Nian, Gao Anagong, Yifu Qian, and others with a host of a hundred thousand to attack him; they raised earthen hills, bored more than seventy holes into the wall, and dammed the river water to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Luji shut the city gates and held firm; Qian sent his generals Daxi Nian, Gao Anagong, Yifu Qian, and others at the head of a hundred thousand men to attack him; they raised earthen hills, bored more than seventy holes in the wall, and dammed the river to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 勣時戰士不過二千，晝夜相拒。

translations.literal: At that time Luji's fighting men numbered no more than two thousand, and day and night they faced one another in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Luji had no more than two thousand fighting men, and day and night they held the enemy at bay.

sentences.zh: 經四旬，勢漸迫。

translations.literal: After forty days the situation grew gradually pressing.
translations.idiomatic: After forty days the situation grew increasingly desperate.

sentences.zh: 勣於是出奇兵擊之，斬數千級，降二千人。

translations.literal: Luji thereupon sent extraordinary troops to strike them, beheaded several thousand, and received the surrender of two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Luji then sent a surprise force against them, killed several thousand, and accepted the surrender of two thousand.

sentences.zh: 梁睿軍且至，賊因而解去。

translations.literal: Liang Rui's army was about to arrive, and the rebels therefore dispersed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Rui's army was about to arrive, and the rebels therefore withdrew.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣開府趙仲卿勞之，詔曰：「勣器識優長，氣調英遠，總馭籓部，風化已行。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke sent open-mansion holder Zhao Zhongqing to comfort him, with an edict saying: "Luji has superior capacity and insight, spirit and bearing heroic and far-reaching; in overall command of the frontier region, transforming influence has already been carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian sent Open Mansion holder Zhao Zhongqing to comfort him, with an edict that read, "Luji possesses superior capacity and insight, with a spirit heroic and far-reaching; governing the frontier region, he has already brought transforming influence to bear."

sentences.zh: 巴蜀稱兵，奄來圍逼，入守出戰，大摧凶醜。

translations.literal: Ba and Shu raised arms; they suddenly came to besiege and press him; he entered to defend and went out to fight, greatly crushing the vicious and ugly.
translations.idiomatic: When Ba and Shu raised arms and suddenly came to besiege him, he defended the city and went out to fight, crushing the rebel forces.

sentences.zh: 貞節雄規，厥功甚茂，可使持節、上柱國。

translations.literal: His steadfast integrity and heroic design—his achievement is very abundant; he may be made Bearer of the Staff and Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: His steadfast integrity and heroic conduct have yielded abundant merit; he is appointed Bearer of the Staff and Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 賜一子爵中山縣公。

translations.literal: One son is granted the title Duke of Zhongshan County.
translations.idiomatic: One son is enfeoffed as Duke of Zhongshan.
(Close of edict.)

sentences.zh: 開皇二年，突厥犯塞，以勣為北道行軍元帥以備邊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang the Turks violated the frontier; Luji was made marching supreme commander of the northern route to guard the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang the Turks raided the frontier; Luji was made marching supreme commander of the northern route to guard the border.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜夏州總管。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed overall commander of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed overall commander of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 上以其家世貴盛，勳效克彰，甚重之。

translations.literal: The emperor because his family for generations was noble and flourishing and his meritorious achievements were clearly manifest greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family had been noble and flourishing for generations and his achievements were clearly manifest, the emperor greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 後為漢王諒納勣女為妃，恩遇彌厚。

translations.literal: Later the Prince of Han, Liang, took Luji's daughter as consort, and favor and treatment grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Prince of Han, Liang, took Luji's daughter as consort, and imperial favor toward the family grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔曰：「上柱國、楚國公勣，蜀人寇亂之日，稱兵犯順，固守金湯，隱如敵國。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict said: "Senior Pillar of State and Duke of Chu state Luji, on the day when Shu people raided in disorder, raised troops in violation of obedience, firmly held metal and boiling water defenses, and stood hidden like a rival state."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict read, "Senior Pillar of State and Duke of Chu Luji, on the day when the people of Shu rose in rebellion, took up arms in defiance of the throne, held his defenses firm as metal and boiling water, and stood like a rival state."

sentences.zh: 嘉猷大節，其勞已多，可食始州臨津縣邑千戶。

translations.literal: His excellent plans and great integrity—his labors have already been many; he may receive the fief of a thousand households in Linjin County, Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His excellent counsel and great integrity have already cost him much labor; he is granted a fief of a thousand households in Linjin County, Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 」十年，以疾征還京師，詔諸王並至勣第，中使顧問，道路不絕。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was summoned back to the capital on account of illness; an edict ordered all the princes to come to Luji's residence, palace envoys to inquire after him—the road was unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was recalled to the capital on account of illness; an edict ordered all the princes to visit Luji's residence, and palace envoys came in an unbroken stream to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，時年五十五。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 上悼惜者久之，特加賵贈，鴻臚監護喪事，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned and cherished his memory for a long time, specially increased funeral gifts, had the Court of Diplomatic Reception oversee the funeral, and gave the posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him for a long time, granted special funeral gifts, had the Court of Diplomatic Reception oversee the funeral, and gave him the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子賢嗣，官至顯州刺史、大理少卿、武賁郎將。

translations.literal: His son Xian succeeded and reached the posts of Governor of Xianzhou, Vice Minister of Justice, and Valiant Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian succeeded him and rose to Governor of Xianzhou, Vice Minister of Justice, and Valiant Guard General.

sentences.zh: 賢弟毓。

translations.literal: Xian's younger brother Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's younger brother was Yu.

sentences.zh: 子毓毓字道生，少英果，有氣節。

translations.literal: His son Yu, styled Daosheng, from youth was heroic and resolute and possessed spirit and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu, whose courtesy name was Daosheng, was from youth heroic and resolute and possessed real integrity.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒出鎮并州，毓以妃兄為王府主簿。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Han, Liang, went out to garrison Bingzhou, Yu as elder brother of the consort served as chief clerk of the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Han, Liang, went out to garrison Bingzhou, Yu served as chief clerk of the princely establishment as the consort's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 從趙仲卿北征突厥，以功授儀同三司。

translations.literal: He followed Zhao Zhongqing in the northern campaign against the Turks and for merit was appointed Companion of the Heir, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhao Zhongqing in the northern campaign against the Turks and, for his merit, was appointed Companion of the Heir, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩，煬帝即位，征諒入朝。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke died and Emperor Yang took the throne, Liang was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian died and Emperor Yang took the throne, Liang was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 諒納諮議王頍之謀，發兵作亂。

translations.literal: Liang adopted the counsel of Adviser Wang Yi and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Liang adopted the counsel of Adviser Wang Yi and raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 毓苦諫不從，因謂弟懿曰：「吾匹馬歸朝，自得免禍。

translations.literal: Yu remonstrated bitterly but was not followed; he therefore said to his younger brother Yi: "If I return to court alone on one horse, I shall naturally escape disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Yu remonstrated bitterly but was not heeded; he therefore said to his younger brother Yi, "If I return to court alone, I can escape disaster."

sentences.zh: 此乃身計，非為國也。

translations.literal: This is a plan for my person, not for the state.
translations.idiomatic: That is a plan for my own safety, not for the state.

sentences.zh: 今且偽從，以思後計。

translations.literal: For now I shall feign compliance in order to think of a later plan.
translations.idiomatic: For now I shall feign compliance while I think of a later plan.

sentences.zh: 」毓兄顯州刺史賢言于帝曰：「臣弟毓素懷志節，必不從亂，但逼凶威，不能克遂。

translations.literal: Yu's elder brother, Xianzhou Governor Xian, spoke to the emperor saying: "Your subject's younger brother Yu has long cherished integrity and will surely not follow the rebellion, but pressed by fierce authority he cannot bring his purpose to completion."
translations.idiomatic: Yu's elder brother, Governor of Xianzhou Xian, said to the emperor, "My younger brother Yu has long cherished integrity and will surely not join the rebellion, but pressed by Liang's power he cannot yet act."

sentences.zh: 臣請從軍，與毓為表裡，諒不足圖也。

translations.literal: Your subject requests to follow the army and act with Yu as outer and inner—Liang is not worth plotting against.
translations.idiomatic: I request permission to join the army and act with Yu from within and without—Liang can easily be overthrown.

sentences.zh: 」帝以為然，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this right and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 賢密遣家人齎敕書至毓所，與之計議。

translations.literal: Xian secretly sent a household member bearing an imperial patent to Yu's place to plan with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian secretly sent a household member bearing an imperial edict to Yu's quarters to plan with him.

sentences.zh: 諒出城，將往介州，令毓與總管屬硃濤留守。

translations.literal: Liang went out of the city, was about to proceed to Jiezhou, and ordered Yu and the overall commander's subordinate Zhu Tao to remain and garrison the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liang left the city, intending to proceed to Jiezhou, and ordered Yu and the overall commander's subordinate Zhu Tao to remain and hold the city.

sentences.zh: 毓謂濤曰：「漢王構逆，敗不旋踵，吾豈坐受夷滅，孤負家國邪！

translations.literal: Yu said to Tao: "The Prince of Han has plotted rebellion; defeat will come in no time—how could I sit and receive extermination and fail my family and state!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu said to Tao, "The Prince of Han has plotted rebellion; defeat will come swiftly—how can I sit and await destruction and fail my family and state!"

sentences.zh: 當與卿出兵拒之。

translations.literal: I must join with you in leading troops out to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: I must join you in leading troops out to resist him.

sentences.zh: 」濤驚曰：「王以大事相付，何得有是語！

translations.literal: Tao was alarmed and said: "The prince entrusted you with a great matter—how can there be such words!"
translations.idiomatic: Tao was alarmed and said, "The prince entrusted you with a great matter—how can you speak such words!"

sentences.zh: 」因拂衣而去。

translations.literal: He thereupon brushed his robes and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon brushed off his robes and left.

sentences.zh: 毓追斬之。

translations.literal: Yu pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pursued and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 時諒司馬皇甫誕前以諫諒被囚，毓於是出誕，與之協計，及開府、磐石侯宿勤武，開府宇文永昌，儀同成端、長孫愷，車騎、安成侯元世雅，原武令皇甫文顥等，閉城拒諒。

translations.literal: At that time Liang's marshal Huangfu Dan had earlier been imprisoned for remonstrating with Liang; Yu thereupon released Dan and planned with him, together with open-mansion holder and Marquis of Panshi Su Qinwu, open-mansion holder Yuwen Yongchang, Companions of the Heir Cheng Duan and Zhangsun Kai, Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Ancheng Yuan Shiya, Yuanwu Magistrate Huangfu Wenhao, and others, to close the city and resist Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liang's marshal Huangfu Dan had been imprisoned for remonstrating with him; Yu released Dan and planned with him, together with Open Mansion holder and Marquis of Panshi Su Qinwu, Open Mansion holder Yuwen Yongchang, Companions of the Heir Cheng Duan and Zhangsun Kai, Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Ancheng Yuan Shiya, Yuanwu Magistrate Huangfu Wenhao, and others, to shut the city and resist Liang.

sentences.zh: 部分未定，有人告諒，諒襲擊之。

translations.literal: The disposition of forces was not yet settled when someone informed Liang, and Liang launched a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Before the disposition of forces was settled, someone informed Liang, and Liang launched a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 毓見諒至，紿其眾曰：「此賊軍也。

translations.literal: When Yu saw Liang arrive he deceived his troops saying: "These are rebel troops."
translations.idiomatic: When Yu saw Liang arrive he deceived his troops, saying, "These are rebel troops."

sentences.zh: 」諒攻城南門，毓時遣稽胡守堞，稽胡不識諒，射之，箭下如雨。

translations.literal: Liang attacked the south gate; Yu at that time had Jiehu guarding the battlements; the Jiehu did not recognize Liang and shot at him—arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Liang attacked the south gate; Yu had Jiehu tribesmen guarding the battlements; they did not recognize Liang and shot at him—arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 諒復至西門，守兵皆并州人，素識諒，即開門納之。

translations.literal: Liang came again to the west gate; the garrison troops were all men of Bingzhou, had long known Liang, and at once opened the gate to admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang came again to the west gate; the garrison troops were all men of Bingzhou who knew Liang well and at once opened the gate to admit him.

sentences.zh: 毓遂見害，時年二十八。

translations.literal: Yu was thereupon killed, aged twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was thereupon killed, at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 及諒平，煬帝下詔曰：「褒顯名節，有國通規，加等飾終，抑推令典。

translations.literal: When Liang was pacified Emperor Yang issued an edict saying: "To praise and display integrity and principle is the common rule of a state; to add rank in adorning the end is rather to push forward the excellent standard."
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was pacified, Emperor Yang issued an edict saying, "To praise and display integrity is the common rule of a state; to add rank in honoring the dead is to uphold the excellent standard."

sentences.zh: 毓深識大義，不顧姻親，出於萬死，首建奇策。

translations.literal: Yu deeply understood great righteousness, did not consider marriage kin, emerged from ten thousand deaths, and first established a wondrous stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yu deeply understood the greater cause, set aside family ties, risked death, and was first to devise a bold stratagem.

sentences.zh: 去逆歸順，殉義亡身，追加榮命，宜優恆禮。

translations.literal: He left rebellion and returned to obedience, died for righteousness and lost his person—adding posthumous glory and rank should follow the constant rites with excellence.
translations.idiomatic: He left rebellion and returned to loyalty, died for righteousness, and deserves posthumous honors in accordance with the highest rites.

sentences.zh: 可贈大將軍，封正義縣公，賜帛二千匹，諡曰湣。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Great General, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhengyi County, given two thousand bolts of silk, and given the posthumous name Min.
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously appointed Great General, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhengyi, granted two thousand bolts of silk, and given the posthumous name Min.
(Close of edict.)

sentences.zh: 子願師嗣，尋拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Yuanshi succeeded and was soon appointed Companion of the Heir, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanshi succeeded him and was soon appointed Companion of the Heir, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 大業初，行新令，五等並除。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye the new ordinances were enacted and all five ranks were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye reign the new ordinances were enacted and all five ranks of nobility were abolished.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝復下詔曰：「故大將軍、正義湣公毓，臨節能固，捐生殉國，成為令典，沒世不忘。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor again issued an edict saying: "The late Great General and Duke of Zhengyi Min Gong Yu, facing integrity able to hold firm, gave his life and died for the state—this has become an excellent standard, not forgotten after death."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor again issued an edict saying, "The late Great General and Duke of Zhengyi Min, Yu, held firm to his integrity, gave his life for the state, and has become an enduring exemplar that shall not be forgotten."

sentences.zh: 象賢無墜，德隆必祀，改封雍丘湣侯，復以願師承襲。

translations.literal: To image the worthy without letting it fall, where virtue is lofty sacrifice is certain—he is re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongqiu Min, and Yuanshi again inherits the succession.
translations.idiomatic: As the worthy must be honored and virtue long remembered, he is re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongqiu Min, and Yuanshi again inherits the title.

sentences.zh: 」大業末，授千牛左右。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was appointed Left Guard of the Thousand Oxen.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign he was appointed Left Guard of the Thousand Oxen.

sentences.zh: 兄通通字平東，勣之兄也，一名會。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tong, styled Pingdong, was Luji's elder brother, also named Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Tong, whose courtesy name was Pingdong, was Luji's elder brother and was also known as Hui.

sentences.zh: 弘厚有器局。

translations.literal: He was magnanimous and generous with capacity and vision.
translations.idiomatic: He was magnanimous and possessed real capacity and vision.

sentences.zh: 在周，少以父功，賜爵臨貞縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Under Zhou, in youth on his father's merit he was granted the title Marquis of Linzhen County with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou, in youth on his father's merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linzhen with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋授大都督，俄遷儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Great Commander and shortly transferred to Companion of the Heir, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Great Commander and shortly transferred to Companion of the Heir, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰宇文護引之令督親信兵，改封沃野縣公，邑四千七百戶。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Works Yuwen Hu brought him in to command trusted troops, re-enfeoffed him as Duke of Woye County with a fief of four thousand seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Works Yuwen Hu brought him in to command trusted troops and re-enfeoffed him as Duke of Woye with a fief of four thousand seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後加開府，歷武賁中大夫、北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was given open mansion and served in succession as Central Grand Master of the Valiant Guard and Governor of Northern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given Open Mansion and served in turn as Central Grand Master of the Valiant Guard and Governor of Northern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，尉迥作逆，遣其所署莒州刺史烏丸尼率眾來攻。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke was chancellor, Yuwen Yong rose in rebellion and sent his appointed Juzhou Governor Wuwanni leading a host to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chancellor, Yuwen Yong rose in rebellion and sent his appointed Governor of Juzhou, Wuwanni, at the head of a host to attack.

sentences.zh: 通逆擊，破之。

translations.literal: Tong met them in counterattack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Tong met them in counterattack and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 賜物八百段，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: He was given eight hundred lengths of goods and advanced to Great General.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted eight hundred lengths of goods and promoted to Great General.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，進爵南陳郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was advanced in rank to Duke of Nanchen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang reign he was advanced to Duke of Nanchen.

sentences.zh: 尋征入朝，以本官典宿衛。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to court and with his existing office headed the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to court and, in his existing office, headed the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，出拜定州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he went out and was appointed Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was sent out as Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後轉相州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尚高祖妹昌樂長公主，自是恩禮漸隆。

translations.literal: He married the Grand Duke's younger sister, the Princess of Changle, and from this favor and courtesy gradually grew eminent.
translations.idiomatic: He married Yang Jian's younger sister, the Princess of Changle, and from that point imperial favor toward him gradually grew.

sentences.zh: 遷夏州總管、洪州總管。

translations.literal: He was moved to overall commander of Xiazhou and overall commander of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to overall commander of Xiazhou and overall commander of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 所在之職，並稱寬惠。

translations.literal: In every post he held he was called generous and kind.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held he was praised for generosity and kindness.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒官，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died in office, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died in office, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 諡曰安。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was An.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name An.

sentences.zh: 有子寬。

translations.literal: He had a son Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Kuan.

sentences.zh: 賀若誼賀若誼字道機，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: He Ruoyi, styled Daoji, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruoyi, whose courtesy name was Daoji, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖伏連，魏雲州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fulian was Governor of Yunzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fulian had served as Governor of Yunzhou under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父統，右衛將軍。

translations.literal: His father Tong was General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong had served as General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 誼性剛果，有幹略。

translations.literal: Yi was by nature stern and resolute and possessed strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was stern and resolute by nature and possessed real strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 在魏以功臣子賜爵容城縣男。

translations.literal: Under Wei, as son of a meritorious minister, he was granted the title Baron of Rongcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei, as the son of a meritorious minister, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Rongcheng.

sentences.zh: 累遷直閤將軍、大都督、通直散騎常侍、尚食典禦。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to General of the Direct Gate, Great Commander, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Director of the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to General of the Direct Gate, Great Commander, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 周太祖據有關中，引之左右。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder held Guanzhong he brought Yi to his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai held Guanzhong he brought Yi into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 嘗使詣杏城，屬茹茹種落摧貳，屯於河表。

translations.literal: He was once sent to Xingcheng; at that time Ruru tribal groups were broken and divided, encamped on the north bank of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He was once sent to Xingcheng; at that time Ruru tribal groups were divided and encamped on the north bank of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 誼因譬以禍福，誘令歸附，降者萬餘口。

translations.literal: Yi by parable of fortune and disaster induced them to submit in allegiance, and more than ten thousand submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi persuaded them with talk of fortune and disaster and induced them to submit; more than ten thousand came over.

sentences.zh: 太祖深奇之，賜金銀百兩。

translations.literal: The founder deeply marveled at this and gave him a hundred taels of gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai was deeply impressed and granted him a hundred taels of gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 齊遣其舍人楊暢結好於茹茹，太祖恐其並力，為邊境之患，使誼聘茹茹。

translations.literal: Qi sent its Retainer Yang Chang to form friendly ties with the Ruru; the founder feared they would combine strength and become a frontier trouble and sent Yi on a mission to the Ruru.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent its retainer Yang Chang to form ties with the Ruru; Yuwen Tai feared they would combine forces and become a frontier threat, and sent Yi on a mission to the Ruru.

sentences.zh: 誼因啖以厚利，茹茹信之，遂與周連和，執暢付誼。

translations.literal: Yi by feeding them thick profit won their trust; the Ruru thereupon joined in alliance with Zhou and handed Chang over to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi tempted them with rich rewards; the Ruru trusted him, joined in alliance with the Zhou, and handed Chang over to Yi.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司、略陽公府長史。

translations.literal: The founder praised this and appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry, Companion of the Heir Third Rank, and Chief Clerk of the Duke of Lueyang's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai praised this and appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry, Companion of the Heir, Third Rank, and Chief Clerk of the Duke of Lueyang's establishment.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝受禪，除司射大夫，改封霸城縣子，轉左宮伯，尋加開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Zhou received the abdication he was made Grand Master of Archery, re-enfeoffed as Viscount of Bacheng County, transferred to Left Palace Chief, and soon given open mansion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Zhou took the throne, he was appointed Grand Master of Archery, re-enfeoffed as Viscount of Bacheng, transferred to Left Palace Chief, and soon given Open Mansion.

sentences.zh: 後曆靈邵二州刺史，原信二州總管，俱有能名。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as governor of Ling and Shao provinces and overall commander of Yuan and Xin provinces, all with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in turn as governor of Ling and Shao provinces and overall commander of Yuan and Xin provinces, earning a reputation for ability in each post.

sentences.zh: 其兄敦，為金州總管，以讒毀伏誅。

translations.literal: His elder brother Dun, overall commander of Jinzhou, was executed on account of slander.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Dun, overall commander of Jinzhou, was executed on account of slander.

sentences.zh: 坐是免職。

translations.literal: On this account he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: On this account he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總萬機，召誼治熊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs he summoned Yi to govern as Governor of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of government affairs he summoned Yi to serve as Governor of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 平齊之役，誼率兵出函谷，先據洛陽，即拜洛州刺史，進封建威縣侯。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Qi, Yi led troops out through Hangu Pass, first seized Luoyang, was at once appointed Governor of Luozhou, and advanced to Marquis of Jianwei County.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign to pacify Qi, Yi led troops out through Hangu Pass, seized Luoyang first, was at once appointed Governor of Luozhou, and advanced to Marquis of Jianwei.

sentences.zh: 齊范陽王高紹義之奔突厥也，誼以兵追之，戰于馬邑，遂擒紹義。

translations.literal: When the Qi Prince of Fanyang, Gao Shaoyi, fled to the Turks, Yi with troops pursued him, fought at Mayi, and thereupon captured Shaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi Prince of Fanyang, Gao Shaoyi, fled to the Turks, Yi pursued him with troops, fought at Mayi, and captured Shaoyi.

sentences.zh: 以功進位大將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Great General.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Great General.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，拜亳州總管，馳驛之部。

translations.literal: When the Grand Duke was chancellor he was appointed overall commander of Bozhou and galloped by post relay to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chancellor he was appointed overall commander of Bozhou and galloped by post relay to take up his command.

sentences.zh: 西遏司馬消難，東拒尉迥。

translations.literal: West he blocked Sima Xiaonan; east he resisted Yuwen Yong.
translations.idiomatic: To the west he blocked Sima Xiaonan; to the east he resisted Yuwen Yong.

sentences.zh: 申州刺史李慧反，誼討之，進爵范陽郡公，授上大將軍。

translations.literal: Shenzhou Governor Li Hui rebelled; Yi campaigned against him, was advanced to Duke of Fanyang commandery, and appointed Senior Great General.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhou Governor Li Hui rebelled; Yi campaigned against him, was advanced to Duke of Fanyang, and appointed Senior Great General.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，入為右武候將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he entered service as General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang reign he entered service as General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 河間王弘北征突厥，以誼為副元師。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hejian, Hong, campaigned north against the Turks and made Yi deputy supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hejian, Hong, campaigned north against the Turks and appointed Yi deputy supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 軍還，轉左武候大將軍。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was transferred to General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was transferred to General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: On account of an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜華州刺史，俄轉敷州刺史，改封海陵郡公，復轉涇州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Governor of Huazhou, soon transferred to Governor of Fuzhou, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Hailing commandery, and again transferred to Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed Governor of Huazhou, soon transferred to Governor of Fuzhou, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Hailing, and again transferred to Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為邊患，朝廷以誼素有威名，拜靈州刺史，進位柱國。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly became a frontier trouble; the court because Yi had long possessed a reputation for might appointed him Governor of Lingzhou and advanced him to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier; because Yi had long possessed a reputation for might, the court appointed him Governor of Lingzhou and promoted him to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 誼時年老，而筋力不衰，猶能重鎧上馬，甚為北夷所憚。

translations.literal: Yi was then old in years, yet his sinew and strength did not decline; he could still don heavy armor and mount a horse, and the northern barbarians deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was then advanced in years, yet his strength had not declined; he could still don heavy armor and mount a horse, and the northern peoples deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 數載，上表乞骸骨，優詔許之。

translations.literal: After several years he submitted a memorial requesting to yield his bones; a gracious edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; a gracious edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 誼家富於財，於郊外構一別廬，多植果木。

translations.literal: Yi's household was rich in wealth; in the suburbs he built a separate lodge and planted many fruit trees.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's household was wealthy; in the suburbs he built a separate lodge and planted many fruit trees.

sentences.zh: 每邀賓客，列女樂，遊集其間。

translations.literal: He regularly invited guests, arrayed female musicians, and gathered for pleasure within it.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly invited guests, set out female musicians, and gathered for pleasure there.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，時年七十七。

translations.literal: He died at home, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home, at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 子舉襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Ju inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ju inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 庶長子協，官至驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His eldest son by a concubine, Xie, reached the post of General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son by a concubine, Xie, rose to General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 協弟祥，奉車都尉。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Xiang was Commandant of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's younger brother Xiang served as Commandant of the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 祥弟與，車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Xiang's younger brother Yu was General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's younger brother Yu served as General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 誼兄子弼，別有傳。

translations.literal: Yi's nephew Bi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's nephew Bi has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 史評史臣曰：于義、竇榮定等，或南陽姻亞，或豐邑舊遊，運屬時來，俱宣力用。

translations.literal: The historian's appraisal: the historiographer says: Yu Yi, Dou Rongding, and others—some were marriage kin of Nanyang, some were old companions of Fengyi—when fortune matched the times arriving, all displayed their strength in service.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's appraisal: the historiographer writes: Yu Yi, Dou Rongding, and the others—some were marriage kin from Nanyang, some were old companions from Fengyi—when fortune favored the times, all displayed their talents in service.

sentences.zh: 以勞定國，以功懋賞，保其祿位，貽厥子孫。

translations.literal: By labor they settled the state, by achievement they received abundant reward, preserved their stipends and posts, and bequeathed them to their sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: By their labor they helped settle the state, by their achievements they received rich rewards, preserved their stipends and offices, and passed them on to their descendants.

sentences.zh: 析薪克荷，崇基弗墜，盛矣！

translations.literal: Splitting firewood they were able to bear it; the lofty foundation did not fall—how flourishing!
translations.idiomatic: Their sons were able to bear the burden; the lofty foundation did not fall—how flourishing indeed!

sentences.zh: 豆盧毓遇屯剝之機，亡身殉義；

translations.literal: Dou Lu Yu met the moment of difficulty and stripping, lost his person and died for righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Lu Yu met a time of peril and stripping away, and gave his life for righteousness;

sentences.zh: 陰世師遭天之所廢，捨命不渝。

translations.literal: Yin Shishi encountered what Heaven had cast aside and gave up his life without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shishi encountered a dynasty Heaven had cast aside and gave up his life without wavering.

sentences.zh: 使夫死者有知，足以無愧君親矣。

translations.literal: Had the dead possessed knowledge, it would have been enough to be without shame before ruler and kin.
translations.idiomatic: Had the dead possessed awareness, they would have had no cause for shame before ruler and kin.
